title: An editor reads the CLI's own documents: `nvs check --json` at version 1, the test report at version 2 with every record located, and a Test Explorer that is those two projected
scope:
the two machine-readable surfaces the editor layer consumes — `nvs check --json` and
`nvs test`'s JSON report, including the discovery document `--list` writes — and the shape of the
VS Code Test Explorer that reads the second. It settles what each document carries and what its
version number means. It says nothing about coverage, which has no data source to wire, and
nothing about when the client lands, which is
`rule:ide/every-feature-is-staged-behind-its-dependency`'s question.
validatedBy:
`tests/conformance/lang/a-test-run-reports-a-versioned-json-document.nvst`,
`tests/conformance/lang/a-test-run-lists-what-it-declares-without-running-it.nvst`, and the named
tests in `crates/nvs-cli/src/runner.rs` and `crates/nvs-cli/tests/check.rs`.

summary.headline: The editor reads the CLI's own documents; the Test Explorer is those shown
summary.body:
Every machine-readable surface an editor needs is a document the command line already writes,
and each is versioned once at its root. `nvs check --json` is at version 1. The test report is
at version 2, where every test carries the file, line and column it is declared at, and `nvs
test --list` writes the same document with no verdicts because nothing ran. The Test Explorer is
built from those two: the list fills the tree, a filtered run fills in results, and the editor
computes nothing the documents do not already say.
